utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gojkovic. Please be seated. Mr. Gojkovic, before we continue I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Lukic will now continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, I just need to take a look at today's transcript. Yesterday at the end of the day, we started discussing documentation from the police that had to do with the demolition of Ferhadija. I should show you a document first, 1D5770. Those are instructions of the Trial Chamber. For the record, let us point out that this document was mentioned in your report: B/C/S pages 65 to 88, and in the English version, pages 74 through 94. Have you seen this criminal file from the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us? Would you like to draw our attention to something in relation to this document? What kind of information did you manage to find? What kind of information did you not manage to find?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were looking for this case for a long, long time. Finally, I managed to get it from the public security centre in Banja Luka. When I took the file, I really read through it, all the witness statements. In addition to the record and the witness statements, there was nothing there. I found nothing, literally. I was there, I heard that, I didn't see anybody, and so on and so forth. That surprised me. Within the file, I did not find a single photograph from the on-site investigation that was carried out by the investigation judge of the basic court in Banja Luka, although in the record itself it says that the scene, the site, was fully photo-documented. I looked at that. I did not find anything in that file, so all the photographs that I took, I took from the Internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what were you told? How did the photographs disappear?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that all the documents were taken by the Office of the Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal and that they have no other documents except for the ones that they gave me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D1179. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, let's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page numbers, you mentioned, Mr. Lukic, were the hard copy page numbers from the report in the attachment to the report, and you now separately --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D1179 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question with respect to this file. Mr. Gojkovic, you said: "Finally I managed to get it from the public security centre in Banja Luka." When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. I can find that. I'll tell you right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Approximately. Are you now looking at your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's around the 28th of August, Jovica Roguljic gave this to me, head of department in Banja Luka. Although the -- he had this from the Ministry of Justice and then they returned it to them, and then the centre to me, and I signed for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said 28th of August. Which year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2014. Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- what you've got here is that on the 1st of September, 2014, again I went to see Jovica Roguljic. I don't know exactly when he gave this to me, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I'm fine. You have answered my question. Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You can find it in the report. There are cover letters, page 72, 71 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I just wanted to have the date on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 1D5771 now on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you recognise this document, Mr. Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The destruction of the Petricevac monastery. No, no, no, sorry. No. Yes, of Saint Ante.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain this documentation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From who and when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same way as I did for the Ferhadija, and at the same time and from the same man.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the situation regarding the information that was contained in this document? What did you find and what did you not find?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately the same. Although here, I mean, the witnesses here spoke more about the destruction of the buildings around this place and how the glass panes were shattered. The public security station of Budzak was involved here. They carried out the on-site investigation. That is what is written in these statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about photographs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No photographs again. And also the statement in the MUP that the rest of the file was taken over by The Hague OTP. I photocopied everything that I found in the file and I submitted it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the record, in the report of Mr. Gojkovic, this is on pages 89 through 104 in B/C/S, and in the English version pages 95 through 110, and we would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit D1180. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1180 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Gojkovic. Now we're just going to take a look at two more documents and then we'll be done with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First we need 65 ter 16559. That's a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First, I'm going to ask you whether you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the document?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please speak into the microphone. Could all other microphones be switched off. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're invited to speak into the microphone, or perhaps the microphone can be slightly adjusted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, it's all right. It's all right. I received this document in Nova Topola near Gradiska where my command post was, where I was commander at the time. At that time, I did not know about any problems concerning the destruction of religious buildings. At that time in that area where I was based, there was no destruction of religious buildings. I called the command in. We had a meeting. We analysed this. I gave certain instructions, and that's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature at the end of the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Talic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at a document that comes after this one. So this one is dated the 23rd of June, 1992. Now let us take a look at 65 ter, Prosecution number, 16556. The document is dated the 3rd of August, 1992. Again, it says repeated warning against demolition of places of worship. It is type-signed: General -- Major-General Momir Talic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the rest of Mr. Lukic' question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is different. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you started an answer before Mr. Lukic had finished his question. Mr. Lukic, could we restart. Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- repeat your question and then we'll hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the signature of the then-assistant for morale, religious, and legal affairs, Milutin Vukelic. He signed it on behalf of General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you remember if you received this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us received these documents as unit commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you inform the command cadre of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We didn't look at the second page in the first document, but let's look at the second page of this one. It says: "Distribution."

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 1st Engineers Regiment, the 1st Pontoon Battalion in the first, third, sixth, and seventh place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. And was this acted upon, as far as you know, because in the document all the unit commanders are warned to prevent irresponsible acts, i.e., the destruction of religious buildings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I noticed in reporting to General Talic who held meetings with the unit commanders, and it is also my opinion that he was a person of authority, I don't know a commanding officer of any of these units who would violate his order. Perhaps there were such instances, but if they this read it, that would not have been very likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer those two documents into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we first go back to the first page of this document, because I would have an additional question. Mr. Gojkovic, a reference is made to instances of demolition of places of worship that were still witnessed. Could you tell us whether you have any knowledge about what was observed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know - I wasn't there - the first buildings that were destroyed were in the area of the Prijedor municipality. And then later when combat started, there were these stories in Kotor Varos. I was on good terms with Colonel Kosanovic, the commander of the regiment, who I replaced. And even one thing, I think Commander Milutin Vukelic and Hasanovic came to me at the end of June, and they wrote the draft of that order while they were with me in the area of Nova Topola. They were very disappointed and they were trying to find a way of resolving this situation, and I think that all of these orders were initiated by Colonel --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and he came with me -- to me with Kosanovic because they thought that the engineers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the name of the colonel you referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel Milutin Vukelic and Colonel Lazar Kosanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could I invite you to finish your sentence when you started saying that "because they thought that the engineers ...," and what did you say then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. They first came to us because at that time no one, no one had that much reserve explosives as we did, and they came to see us so -- to check whether any of us would dare to do something like that. They came to see me and I said that my entire explosive reserves were at the central depot. I didn't even need it. Throughout the whole war, I didn't need any of the explosives. And I'm sorry because I couldn't find all this data in the archives to be able to show it. At my command post, they drafted this order, not this one but I think there's another one. I think I can find it here somewhere. Let me see where I put it. I do remember it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could I ask you then -- or did I understand you well that you have no specific knowledge about the instances that apparently triggered this order to be issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not at the time, I didn't have any knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just offer those two documents into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 16559 shall be assigned Exhibit D1181. And the other one, 65 ter number 16556 shall be assigned Exhibit D1182. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1181 and D1182 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I would just offer the report to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objection to it being MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then we'll probably discuss with the Prosecution which parts should be excluded since those documents were admitted separately and they are a part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we'll hear from you later exactly what is still there to be tendered as annexes we have not yet dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if you ask the report to be MFI'd, is that a report including all the annexes or just the report up to where the annexes start? Because they are more or less separated from the report and dealt with separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They are. But it may be that we will keep some annexes and we have to discuss it with the Prosecution. So maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll then MFI the report and we'll later determine what is still attached and what is not attached any further. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just for the clarity of the record, what I understand Mr. Lukic to be asking to be marked for identification is what is currently uploaded as 1D05892, which currently includes both the report and the attachments --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- pending discussions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how it is now. And whether that will change, we'll see that later. So more or less it's more -- it's reserving a number for the report, still to be determined what is part of it and what is not. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit D1183. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1183 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gojkovic, these were all the questions we had for you, and we thank you for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this morning, Mr. Lukic showed you a couple of police files into the destruction of the Ferhadija mosque and the Petricevac church. Did you review those files in the course of preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You apparently are nodding. Could you please clearly state your answer to that question so that it's on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do either of those files reflect anyone being punished for destroying the mosques; that is, convicted and sentenced to a term of years in prison by the war-time Bosnian Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again you're invited to speak into the microphone, if need be, to adjust it, so that your words will not be lost.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. As far as I can see, the case is still in the court. The documents that I found in the case file do not allow me to conclude whether somebody was convicted or not because the case has not been completed. No judgement either at first instance or second instance has been handed down yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Lukic also showed you an order this morning where General Talic said, among other things, that if anyone in the 1st Krajina Corps destroyed a mosque it could be considered a criminal act and measures would be taken. You're not aware of any soldier in the 1st Krajina Corps being convicted and sentenced in the Banja Luka military court for destroying a mosque or a Catholic church, are you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But during the war in the B and H, there was the military court of the Army of Republika Srpska. I could not have access to those cases, so I don't know what those judgements were. I did not deal with that. I dealt exclusively with these two buildings. You also had the military court. I did ask about documents of the military court, but I could not have access to them. Those documents were taken away --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this Chamber has received the register of the Banja Luka military court. What I'm asking for the moment isn't what you analysed in the course of preparing your report. You provide a lot of information, both the last two days and in your report, from your personal knowledge. You're not personally aware of any soldier in the 1st Krajina Corps being punished for destroying a mosque or a Catholic church during the war, are you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying again: If there were such reports, they probably ended up at the military court of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there. What Mr. Traldi asked you, whether you have any knowledge, not whether such information could possibly be found somewhere, but whether you have any personal knowledge about prosecutions, convictions, and sentenced soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you and General Talic both, from your training in the JNA, you knew it was illegal, a violation of the international laws of war, to destroy religious buildings; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about your report. As an initial matter, you note on page 41 of the English and 39 of the B/C/S and you discussed yesterday that you and four other people were involved in drafting the report. Which sections did you draft yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which parts? Well, other than gathering the data about the engineer units of the VRS, and other than analysing the VOB-8 of both of the units, everything else did myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Attachment P which we discussed briefly and Mr. Lukic showed you yesterday, the entry for Donji Kamengrad Grad, the mosque in Donji Kamengrad that was destroyed, did you also do that section yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the mosque in Kamengrad? I don't understand. In what sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure. Let me rephrase. Attachment P consists of about 40 to 50 entries for individual mosques, one of which Mr. Lukic showed you yesterday related to the mosque in Donji Kamengrad Grad. Did you do that section of the report yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You would have selected which photographs to use yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of the 94 mosques that were looked at here, I took the most characteristic ones that were of most interest to me, but it's a system of destruction without any order at all. Through those mosques, I could practically show --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I object. There is no need for yelling in this courtroom. This is the third time that my colleague is yelling at the witness. There is no need for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi is invited to use his voice in such a way that the witness will not feel in any way intimidated. And the witness is invited to focus his answer on the question as put to him. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, the photographs in Attachment P, you selected those yourself; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the text in Attachment P, how did you create that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you read it to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, there are 40 entries in Attachment P. 40 to 50. Let's look at one. Can we have --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, could you just tell me that one that you referred to just now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to call it up on the screen, sir, and we'll have it front of you in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 1D05892, the tendered report. And I'm looking for page 149 in the English, 142 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you give the number again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's D1183, MFI, now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is your entry on the Carsijska mosque in Srebrenica town; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said it was the mosque in Kamengrad in Sanski Most. Now this is a completely different mosque, the one in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There are a number of examples, some of which I will refer to, some of which I will call up. This one is your entry, as I put to you a moment ago, on the Carsijska mosque in Srebrenica town; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you please clarify with the witness why we have in the B/C/S an additional photograph in the middle which doesn't appear in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, sir, why do we have an additional photograph in the B/C/S that's not in the English?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know absolutely what you're asking me. I simply reduced a number of photographs that were not important to me that didn't show anything. I didn't want to conceal anything. All I wanted to do was to simplify things using the photographs that I was showing here. I didn't do it just in the case of this mosque. I did it in each of -- with each of the mosques. I just wanted to simplify the case that I was working on. I didn't wish to conceal anything, and you cannot conceal anything because you also have that in your own case file.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll see how you simplified it in a moment. Before we do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Witness, could you tell us did you prepare the English version of the report yourself as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How, then, could you simplify matters? Did you give instructions to someone to leave out photographs or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: May I try to clarify it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, when you say you simplified the photographs, what you mean is this is a subset of the photographs that are used in Mr. Riedlmayer's formatted entry for the same site; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as you didn't prepare the English, do you have any knowledge why the photograph in the middle of the page in the B/C/S would be present in the B/C/S but not in the English?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that the Defence accepted what I did and that's what they presented. That's my opinion. Perhaps I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No personal knowledge as to why the middle photograph isn't in the English, right; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You have no personal knowledge as to why the middle photograph in the B/C/S is present in the B/C/S but not in the English, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying again for me to analyse any destroyed building, the photographs that I presented are quite sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, respectfully --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I showed was quite sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- I'm going to stop you. This is the fourth time I'm asking you the same yes or no question. There's, in the middle of the page in the B/C/S, a single photograph that Judge Fluegge had originally asked you about -- sorry, I think Judge Fluegge had originally asked you about, that's present in the B/C/S. It's not present in the English. You yourself don't know why it's present in one and not the other; right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm answering you. I cannot answer with a "yes" or a "no." I personally left it out because I didn't need it for my own analysis. These three photographs were quite sufficient for me to be able to discuss any aspect of the -- this particular building. It was my opinion, I believe, that you cannot really see anything from this photograph, and it's not necessary in order to analyse the destruction of this particular building. These three photographs are quite sufficient for me to be able to talk about --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the things --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that have to do with the destruction of this particular building, and that you can prove quite enough things just on the basis of these three photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Since I triggered the whole discussion, may I just put one additional question to you, Mr. Gojkovic. Look at the left side of the screen. There you have the Serbian version of your report. You find a photograph in the middle. There are three rows: A small photograph on top, one in the middle, and two photographs on the bottom of the page. Why is the photograph in the middle in the Serbian version to be seen? This is your version, I assume, because you didn't prepare the English one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, that's correct, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means you didn't simplify it by taking out the fourth photograph in your version?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please. I wanted to look. I have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That means the photograph is still to be seen in your report. Have you any idea why this photograph disappeared by translating your report into English? Have you any idea about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then you have to ask the Defence about that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That -- that is -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I sent this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I sent this to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This is exactly what Mr. Traldi and I myself wanted to know how that disappeared. Perhaps the Defence should explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are trying to see who was translating it, whether it was our translator or CLSS. So if it's our, we will contact him. If it's CLSS, we have to ask CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This clarifies the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still am a bit confused, Witness. Because, Mr. Gojkovic, you explained to us why three photographs would be enough. Now if you had nothing to do with the translation and if you are saying to us, "Well, ask the Defence," why then did you give such an explanation as to why it would be satisfactory to have only three instead of four if you had nothing to do with the conversion into English? I'm confused by that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just a confusion. I thought that I left the photograph out in my report. It's just a bit of confusion, and I apologise. It's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're telling us that you bear no responsibility and you were not involved in any way in reducing four photographs into three photographs? Your answer may not be clear on the record. Could you please pronounce it properly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply included all the four photographs in my report. I don't know whether the Defence translation or whoever did it here at the secretariat left out one of those photographs, but I had nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, apart from who did it, have you not observed that we have a different English version compared to the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to admit, I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, at temporary transcript page 18 today, lines 14 through 17, you said it was your opinion that you couldn't see anything from this photograph in the middle of the page, that it wasn't necessary, and the other three photographs are quite sufficient. Now, you gave that evidence because you weren't focusing on the question. You were simply trying to justify what you understood to be the reductions in Mr. Riedlmayer's material that you thought you'd made; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's not correct. On the basis of these three photographs, I can see quite clearly how this mosque -- I mean, not absolutely. I wasn't there. I wasn't recording it. I didn't see it. I wasn't there immediately after the explosion, after the demolition. But it's quite clear how --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you one more time --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the demolition was carried out. You can see it on the basis of these three photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You again haven't answered my question. What I'm putting to you is you testified a moment ago that the photograph you included in the middle of the page in your version, the B/C/S version, wasn't necessary. And let me ask you in a very focused way: Is it your evidence today that you included an unnecessary photograph from which you can't really tell anything on this page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, thank God we have a detailed report of the investigating judge and we have photographs. I'm talking about the photographs. I included them because this building was interesting to me, and had there been more photographs I would have included them. On the basis of the photographs, you can just see --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- where the mosque was located. You can see the place where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You agreed a moment ago that this represents your work reducing and you said simplifying Mr. Riedlmayer's formatted entry for the site. So where in your report it refers to this section, this attachment, as consisting of photographs from Kemal Zukic's book, that's not true. This is material you took directly from Riedlmayer's report; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to look at the description of the damage at the top, and you said you were responsible for the text yourself. The description of the damage begins: "At the time the author visited the locality (July 2002), the site of Carsijska Dzamija was empty land in the centre of Srebrenica." Now, you didn't visit this site in 2002, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never claimed that. Where did I say that I was there?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, this is a report you authored. It says the author visited the site. In fact -- and that's not true, the author of your report did not visit this site in July 2002; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I keep telling that you I took information only from the expert report by Riedlmayer. I was not there. I never said any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what you've done is published something under your name that says the author did something. You've not identified in your report that this was Mr. Riedlmayer's material, and you've certainly created the impression with your text that you did things you didn't do; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question has been answered, but we'd nevertheless would like to know what your objection is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for us it's clear what Mr. Gojkovic thought under "author."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is your objection, sir? Something may be clear to you, but that's no basis for an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is suggested that Mr. Gojkovic put something in his report that is not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, but that's not the basis for an objection still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now where -- Witness, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. In this annex to the report or in your report, where do we find a clear explanation that what you copied here is just the comments of Mr. Riedlmayer and not of you as the author of the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for Riedlmayer's paper, this is just an addition to my report. However, I reduced something. I mean, I paid for all of this. I did all this on my own. I had very little time. Quite simply, I tried, I tried -- I mean, look, it was a big case. I tried to reduce it quite simply. I never said that it was my paper. Look at this now. The municipality of Srebrenica, the city mosque. This paragraph of Riedlmayer's. It's his, not mine. I never made any comment. I just took it at face value. I just left out things that are not important. I did not say whether it was a modern mosque or whether it was a Osmanli mosque or whatever. I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, we're going to look at some of the things you left out after the break. I have a couple of quick remaining questions before hand about this entry. First, you testified yesterday at transcript page 37543 that in your view there was "a lot missing from Mr. Riedlmayer's work." Relative to the individual sites, you yourself have not added anything that you thought was missing to his work; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only dealt with the way in which buildings were demolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Riedlmayer dealt with spirituality, history, and whatever else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me ask -- sir, I'm going to interrupt you. Let me ask very clearly: What is on this page that is not included in Mr. Riedlmayer's entry for the same site? Point me to one thing that is on this page but not in Mr. Riedlmayer's entry?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The page on the screen in front of you. On the screen.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just find it. Let's find it in Riedlmayer's report, and then we'll see. It's hard for me to remember all of that, very hard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In your report, it is page 142.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, see? The Srebrenica municipality, Carsijska Celija, the down-town mosque --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is too fast for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could you please restart your answer but slowly so that the interpreters can interpret your words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Riedlmayer, Your Honours, starts his report about the demolition of this mosque in the following way --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you. What I asked you is point me to one thing that is your entry that is not in Mr. Riedlmayer's. I didn't ask you to read out Mr. Riedlmayer's to us. Point us to one thing that is in your entry on the screen that is not in Mr. Riedlmayer's entry for this site.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My report only contains the first paragraph of Mr. Riedlmayer, where he describes the damage. That is what is of interest to me. Nothing else. So the description of the damage and the photographs. That is the only thing that is of interest to me. I'm not interested in any of the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is there is nothing in your entry that is not in Mr. Riedlmayer's entry, but there are things in his entry that are not in yours; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That text is irrelevant for me and that's why it's not there. For my report, the only thing that is relevant --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- is the description of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we -- we'll take a break very soon, Mr. Traldi. Witness, first of all, in the description of Attachment P you say that these are photographs taken from Mr. Zukic's book. If I understand it well now, it is that photographs -- could you please let me finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kemal Zukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please allow me to finish. First of all, I understand your testimony now to be that the photographs are not taken from that book but are photographs taken from Mr. Riedlmayer's report; that's one. Second, the text to which the brief description of Attachment P refers is not text you drafted but you say is text you copied from Mr. Riedlmayer's report. And I think after -- you agree with that? Could you please say so, whether you agree or not, because otherwise it's lost.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, that's at least my feeling at this moment, that Mr. Traldi, after the break, will focus on whether anything was added or whether anything was left out from Mr. Riedlmayer's text. Mr. Traldi, is that how I have to understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. Although, I had asked a question that I hadn't gotten an answer to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may put that question again, we'll hear the answer, and then take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, there is not anything on this page that is not - no photograph and no part of the description of the damage - that is not also contained in Mr. Riedlmayer's report; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Riedlmayer dealt with lots of things that were irrelevant for my report and that is the basic reason why I left that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, what Mr. Traldi asks you is whether everything we find on this page is also found in Mr. Riedlmayer's report. That's the only thing Mr. Traldi seeks to establish. And I think you answered the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One follow-up, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Consequently, sir, there is nothing on this page that reflects your own analysis or opinion of what happened to this site; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look. I can analyse from photographs what it was that happened here. Everything that Mr. Riedlmayer wrote --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's not the question. The question is whether what we see on this page, that it does not contain any opinion developed by yourself and it is just what you copied from Mr. Riedlmayer's report. Is that correct or is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, that was your last question before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, and I appreciate the Chamber's indulgence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, Mr. Gojkovic. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom, Mr. Lukic, have you found out by now who is responsible for the translation into English of the report of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And that translation was done by CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think what we need is a thorough review of what happened here. And, of course, perhaps, Mr. Traldi, we'll wait for all of your questions. I do not know whether there are any other inconsistencies, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just under the description of damage for this entry, we see a photograph of the mosque which is labelled a pre-war photograph of the mosque; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see the English translation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's in the reverse order to what we are used to. Perhaps we could have B/C/S to the left and English to the right again. There we are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you see the caption to the first photograph, "photograph of the pre-war mosque"; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we now have P2510; page 218 in the English and 219 in the B/C/S. And I think we need the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we again have the usual order; that is, B/C/S to the left, English to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we don't -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's the wrong page in on the right side on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's actually so far --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we are there. Now -- the B/C/S version was right but disappeared now. Now we have the English one on the right side. That should remain. Very good. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: According to my notes, we don't have the page yet in either language. But my notes may be in error. I'm afraid my Ringtail isn't allowing me to double-check. If we could turn back to the beginning of this entry, which should be three pages earlier -- or four pages earlier. And we're on the previous entry on the left which is the entry for Hodovici, and what we need is the beginning of the entry for the Carsijska Dzamija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we're now both in English and in the B/C/S on the previous entry. You just tell us how many pages we should move forward, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 219 in the B/C/S, which I ... and perhaps my speed was off the first time I'd asked, but it's 218 in the English, 219 in the B/C/S, the beginning of the entry for this mosque, and thankfully my notes were right this time. We're on the second page in the English and need to turn back a page. We now have the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what we see before us is the beginning of Mr. Riedlmayer's entry for this site, and in the second paragraph you can read that he mentions that: "In video footage recorded on the 14th of July, 1995, the Carsijska mosque and its minaret were still intact ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could turn now to page 222 in the English, which we've got in the B/C/S but not in the English. We need 222 in the English; 223 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So now we see the same picture that you've identified as the pre-war mosque, and we see that it's clearly identified here as coming from video footage recorded on the 14th of July, 1995 after Srebrenica fell; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So one of the ways that you have simplified, in your words, this entry, is removing the information that the mosque was still standing after the falling of Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, that's not correct. Quite simply, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The information is in Mr. Riedlmayer's entry, it's not in yours, you made that decision. Those things are all true; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment let me take a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, I see you're showing me the entry, sir. You've identified this is a photograph of the pre-war mosque. You've not referred to it correctly as a photograph of the mosque still standing on the 14th of July, 1995, after the fall of Srebrenica. You've removed that information; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe accidentally I wasn't paying attention to that. But that I removed that in order to conceal something, that's ridiculous. Why would I do that when it can be seen from the photograph itself that it is based on footage? There's no need to explain it. Just like what you have. See? It's from several clips that this photograph was created. See?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next page; page 223 in the English and 224 in the B/C/S. Now, this is the photo that you said you'd included in the B/C/S but didn't show anything, wasn't necessary. Mr. Riedlmayer describes this one where you can see the destroyed minaret on the left side in front of the same mosque as being taken on the 19th of July, 1995. You have also simplified this entry by removing that information; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct. You see, this photograph down here on the left --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that's a photograph of the minaret.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're pointing to things on your entry. Point to where it says the minaret was destroyed between the 14th and 19th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you, Mr. Prosecutor, keep saying something that you've already got there. You had this admitted into evidence. That cannot be concealed. I am speaking about the mode of demolition here. That is what I'm interested in. I didn't want to conceal anything here. I did not want to copy everything that Riedlmayer wrote, who said what, and he even gives information here, who was buried, when. That was not the subject of my work. I am speaking only about buildings and the mode of demolition. That's the only thing I'm interested in and that is part of my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You also include in your report an assertion that 10 of the 94 mosques that you purport to discuss were destroyed during combat operations and 84 were destroyed during VRS withdrawal. To make that evaluation -- sorry, were destroyed after VRS withdrawal. To make that evaluation, you would have to evaluate when the mosques were destroyed, the precise information you have removed here; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is precisely the information that I collected from Riedlmayer's report, and I obtained information as to what was demolished in one case and what in the other. Please do the counting and you will reach the same conclusion that I reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We're going to look at a few examples, but let's start with this one. We see that Mr. Riedlmayer's caption - also not included in your report - reflects that media shows that the mosque was destroyed the same day the photo was taken, the 19th of July, 1995. You're aware, of course, that Srebrenica was under VRS control at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you consider this one that was destroyed during combat operations or after VRS withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, I wasn't there. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, no -- sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can accept what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm asking how you came to a conclusion you provide in your expert report for which you provide no support or explanation. You said 10 mosques were destroyed during combat, 84 were destroyed during withdrawal. Was this one of the ones that you say was destroyed during combat or after withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now you're asking me something -- I mean, I cannot remember so many numbers. I went from one building to another and made the tables, and you can see that here. I went from one building to the next, and you can see here that I -- I mean, my time was very short, so I did it afterwards. From the first mosque in Bijeljina in Apacici in July 1992, and then up to the mosque in Srebrenica, Slapovi, in 1995, where I just recorded on the side precisely what Riedlmayer said. I didn't go into whether that was accurate or not. I wasn't even interested in the sources from which he acquired his data.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you're not answering my question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just answering your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, sir. I'm afraid you're not.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps you're not satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My question is: This mosque -- you say 10 during combat, 84 after withdrawal. In which category did you put this one? It is a two-word answer. Please provide it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that in a couple of words. Let's see what Riedlmayer said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, sir. I'm not asking you to look for what Mr. Riedlmayer said. I'm saying, first, you clearly haven't put this mosque in either category; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I looked at 94 mosques. I did not participate in the Srebrenica operation, and I was not an eye-witness to any of those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The other part of what I'm putting to you, sir, is that what you're offering the Trial Chamber is a false dichotomy, that what you're suggesting is the mosques were destroyed either during combat or after withdrawal, and you've excluded information that shows this one was destroyed just after the fighting was over but while the VRS maintained clear control of the area. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how could I know until when the VRS held any town under its control? Where would I get that information from? Who would provide this information to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you didn't know whether --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I -- all I --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, if you didn't know whether the VRS had withdrawn or whether it maintained control, how could you have opined that the destructions took place after VRS withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling you the whole time that what Mr. Riedlmayer wrote, I just put that in the table. Just the data that he presented, nothing more. What he had written.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me be very clear about what I'm putting to you in fairness. You have offered the Trial Chamber in the body of your report unsupported conclusions which you do not explanation and which you now testify you do not know whether they are true or not, and in the attachment, Attachment P, you have included parts of Riedlmayer's work which you do not attribute to him. And to the extent that you've gone anything yourself, it has rendered that attachment less accurate than if you had simply imagine plagiarised it. That's the truth about the report you're offering this Trial Chamber; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you one thing. I -- when I was making this table and the data that I was presenting, I am not going to claim that I'm 100 correct. I might have made some errors. But it's 90 per cent correct, and the data is the data from Mr. Riedlmayer. We can analyse everything. Let's stay here one more day and go mosque by mosque and then we can analyse exactly what it is and come to the truth and see what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you one question between -- you earlier said that the information about dates that you left out as irrelevant was because you were interested in the mode of destruction, not on when it happened. Nevertheless, on page 30 of the English version of your report, I read: "The time when the religious buildings were destroyed, or severely and slightly damaged, is as follows:" So you express an opinion about when that happened. And then after having listed the various months and years, you summarise by saying: "Destruction of religious buildings took place: "* During combat operations ............... 10 buildings "* After VRS withdrawal ................... 84 buildings" What Mr. Traldi apparently is exploring is if you say: "I don't know whether they withdrew or not," how could you possibly qualify 10 as being destroyed during combat operations and 84 buildings after VRS withdrawal if you tell us at the same time that you do not know when the VRS withdrew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I am saying that in Riedlmayer's report he was taking witness statements and they gave the information to him. This is what I'm talking about. Now you would need to read each report for each mosque in order to get that information and that's where I got that information from. I wasn't the one who was doing the analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you not understand your task as an expert who was providing your opinion to do analysis supporting the conclusions that were going to be contained in your report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did that. You take Mr. Riedlmayer's report and you read everything. You would need to read the statements of his witnesses. I took that as a relevant source of information, because that's what he did too. I don't know how accurate they are. I mean, if you're disputing the accuracy of his witness statements, then you can dispute also what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: With that, sir, I'm going to turn away from your purported expert evidence to the factual evidence you provide first about the 1st Krajina Corps' engineering unit. You testified yesterday at transcript page 37533 that if an order for an engineering unit in the 1st Krajina Corps's area of responsibility to destroy something had been passed down the chain of command, you would have been part of that process. Now, that's not true before July 1992, is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where you get the date from and why it would be relevant, the 30th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You provide this broad assertion without a time-period, the commander of the pontoon battalion wouldn't have been part of the chain of command for an order to destroy a building, would he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was your position until July 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, it's the chief of engineers who would have been part of that chain; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You did not hold that position until October 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we 65 ter 32853.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now, sir, to the topic of Muslim and Croat participation in the engineering units of the 1st Krajina Corps. Now, a number of Muslims and Croats were forcibly mobilised into the engineering regiment; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document coming from the command of the 1st Engineers Regiment in Laktasi on the 10th of February 1993. We see it comes from the commander, Major Milan Nastic. At the time --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nastic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the time, who was his immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the professional line, it was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this is a document you would have reviewed yourself; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am seeing it for the first time, but I -- I don't doubt the document. It's his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now under point 2, "Morale of Unit," and it's at the bottom of the page in the B/C/S, and the second bullet point from the bottom in the English, we read: "Combat morale has been particularly affected by the forcible mobilisation of a large number of people, especially Muslims and Croats ..." So in early 1993 Muslims and Croats were forcibly mobilised into the engineering regiment; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it says, then I believe that there was some of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And by that time, the 1st Krajina Corps had taken control of all the territories in its area and a great majority of the Muslim and Croat populations had departed; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which territory are you thinking of here? Is it Laktasi, Banja Luka, the Krajina region?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, the 1st Krajina Corps had control over the Krajina region, it was the part that was its area of responsibility, and most of the Muslims and Croat population that had lived there before the war by this time was gone; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really didn't look into the percentage that is left, but I can tell you something else regarding this document. When a report like this is drafted in the VRS units or the former JNA units, this bullet point about the morale is not something that Nastic wrote. This was written by the -- a doctor who had a PhD in biology. His name was Drago Trkulja, he was the assistant for morale in my unit, and I believe that Nastic didn't read this. The commander didn't read it. Had he read it, he wouldn't have signed it. The man simply wrote that just in order to write something, but it wasn't really relevant. It doesn't say anywhere the actual number of Muslim and Croat soldiers involved here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's -- that's true.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not referred to here, so if you take the date --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you provided, and they were discussed yesterday, lists of Muslims and Croats in the engineering regiment; D1173 and 1174. We've looked at those lists and about 20 per cent of the Muslims and 20 per cent of the Croats who served in the engineering regiment in the entire war begun their service in the unit in the first half of 1993 when this document was drafted. Those people were forcibly mobilised into the unit; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've translated only the part of this document that I have used with the witness, point 2, the morale point. The B/C/S is the full document, and I'd just ask that it be MFI'd for the moment. We'll reduce the B/C/S at the end of the witness's testimony to match the English if nothing else comes up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, no problems with that? Mr. Registrar, would you please assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P7493. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question, Your Honour. I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you had any objections to the document being MFI'd, pending a full translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, it was pending a reduction of the B/C/S to match the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Rather to reduce the B/C/S rather than -- any problem with that for context, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7493 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can just add one thing here. It wasn't just the Muslims and the Croats who were mobilised in 1993. There were people, older people who were mobilised. If we look at the tables, we can see that in that year Serbs, Croats, and Muslims were mobilised. Nobody was targeting Croats and Muslims for mobilisation. I didn't conceal anything in the tables, and the tables and the numbers tell much more than what some assistant for morale wrote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, what was read to you is about forcible -- mobilisation of a large number of people, especially Muslims and Croats, which means that there were others as well. So therefore, that's what already expressed in the document itself. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi. Do you have any personal knowledge about numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I reviewed the figures in the tables very precisely. I didn't conceal anything. Whatever was in the VOBs, VOB-8s, it's also in the tables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I think Mr. Traldi did the same, and he concluded about certain percentages. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did that careful review also reveal that about 15 per cent of the Muslims and 15 per cent of the Croats in your tables never served in the VRS's 1st Engineering Regiment at all because they weren't -- they'd concluded their service, according to the VOB, before the 19th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. That is not correct. I correctly noted down first and last name of those who were in the units until the end of the war. Nothing is concealed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Chamber can see the proportions from the document. Did your careful review reflect that almost 15 per cent of the Muslims were not mobilised until the second half of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, from day one, from the 17th of September when the engineers regiment was formed as a war unit, they were mobilised. They were receiving summons to report to their war-time units. This was the usual manner of mobilising people. There were volunteers but mostly that was the mobilisation system.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me focus very precisely on the information in the VOB. Did your careful review reflect that 15 per cent of the Muslim, about, did not join the engineering regiment according to the document you provided until the second half of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There is continuity. There are Muslims in 1991, 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995 who were in the engineering regiment. At the same time, you have people who are leaving for different reasons. There are those who are deserting, those who are being transferred. It's a living organism. You cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the simple question is whether you agree that 15 per cent of the Muslims which were recorded joined only in the second half of 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that's what is written there, then, yes, that's it. If it's there in the diagram, then I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Judge Orie and Judge Fluegge yesterday asked you about the significance of the ones who began their service on 9th of October, 1995. Now, you first claimed these were volunteers, and then you later testified that a student brigade was mobilised on that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was it the 9th or 29th?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, the truth is these were not volunteers. They were people who were mobilised; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the significance of the date, October 1995, is that at that point the VRS no longer had the overwhelming military superiority it had enjoyed in the Bosnian Krajina in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't put it like that, that it didn't have the overwhelming military power. Had it not had the power, nothing -- it wouldn't have had any successes, so somebody had to have been doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, in 1992 -- let's put it very simply. 1992, the VRS was taking control of territory in the Bosnian Krajina, including Sanski Most and Kljuc. In October 1995, the VRS was losing control of the territory in the Bosnian Krajina, including Sanski Most and Kljuc; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic should not speak aloud and not comment on what is asked, and this is the one, first, and last warning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so where, in 1992, Muslims like the one you mentioned were sent to Belgrade to resolve their status, in 1995, there was a level the desperation and so people that the VRS would never have used in 1992 were being impressed into service. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, all those who were on the list, on the -- of the military conscripts list, were called up. A number of them reported and number of them did not. There is a battalion - an example - that by establishment numbered 860 people, and I had about 276 respond to the first call-up. And in percentages, the same number of Croats, Muslims, and Serbs failed to report. So this did not apply just to one ethnic group. They all had the same -- or they were all thinking along the same lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: About how many people were in the engineering regiment in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read that. 1038.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your VOB reflects that 200 or so Muslims served in the engineering regiment at any point in the war, of which we've just established that half of them were force -- taken together, half of them were either forcibly mobilised in the beginning of 1993, only joined at the end of 1995, or had left before the 19th of May, 1992. So at the most, even based on what we've just discussed, a very, very small percentage of that unit, in 1992, was comprised of Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's there in the table. The forceful mobilisation applied to Serbs, Croats, and Muslims who were in the territory of the municipalities from where the 1st Engineering Regiment was being replenished --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat that last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please repeat your last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbs, Croats, and Muslims were mobilised all in the same way. They were -- each of them tried to evade mobilisation. There were volunteers. I mean, I could have written that in here as well, put in a column indicating the volunteers, but I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And to conclude this topic, sir, you mentioned yesterday a specific person named in the VOB who, on the 10th of July, 1992, you said was sent by the unit to Belgrade. Now, the Chamber has received evidence, and it's P4971 for the parties, that on the 9th of July, 1992, General Mladic issued an order that Muslim and Croat officers should be sent to Belgrade to resolve their status. It's not a coincidence that that's what happened to this man on the 10th of July; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. It's not correct. I was the commander of the engineers regiment at that time. I had sent him to the commander of a battalion. I had sent him to an assignment to work out the rocket positions --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat what he is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, Witness, the interpreters invite you to repeat what you said. You said: "I had sent him to an assignment to work out the rocket positions..." Could you repeat what you then said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the evening, some of his soldiers got drunk and they were going to kill their superior commander who happened to be a Muslim. He avoided that first contact. He escaped to a house. A woman saved him. She hid him. And in the morning he was transferred to the command and then we sent him to Belgrade. It was very difficult for us.
