We were very sorry about all of that. He was a very Goodman and a very good professional, an expert, but it was untenable for us to continue to keep him in the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Threatening to kill a superior commander, that's a serious crime for a soldier to commit; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So if we were to check the log of the Banja Luka military court, we ought to find convictions and long sentences to terms of imprisonment for these people that had made such a threat; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That was reported. Believe me, I didn't follow what happened later. I just know that I detained these people, that they were handed over to the military police, and I think that after a while they returned to the unit. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's because they weren't sentenced to a term of imprisonment. They were taken back into the unit, like huge numbers of other VRS soldiers who committed crimes against Muslims and Croats that the command and military justice system knew about and just sent the same criminals back to the front; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about other cases. I know about this case. It happened there where I was personally, and that's what I could have done myself. As for the state and the system, whether they could have done more and whether they did more, I wasn't following that. Whether they were prosecuted later, I don't know about that. Maybe they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 07036. And I'm turning to a different topic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, could you tell us why this person was sent to Belgrade? For what purpose and what happened to him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite simply to protect him. Later on, he went to third countries. We were on such good terms with him for years. He attended military exercises with us. We were on such good terms, a very positive person in every conceivable respect. There you go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that this positive person who you'd known for years before the war but happened to be a Muslim, he couldn't stay in the unit, he was sent to Belgrade, he was never brought back, and the people who threatened to kill their superior commander for being a Muslim were brought back and accepted into the unit. That's your evidence; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a while, what the consequences were, I mean a month or two later, I really don't know, but I know they were taken away by the military police, you know. Now the question here is whether all of that could have been processed at the time under these circumstances, you know. This Court needs a lot of time to resolve things too, let alone us in a situation of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, let's look at this document, one of the other activities of the 1st Engineering Regiment in 1992. The 1st Engineering Regiment also used people held prisoner at Manjaca camp to labour, for instance, on building fortifications for VRS positions; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see it says Colonel Lazar, and the last name is illegible. That's Colonel Lazar Kosanovic who at the time, the 2nd of October, 1992, was your immediate superior; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not understand what the witness was saying, overlapping speakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to wait for the end of my question. Colonel Lazar, that we see here with the last name illegible, that's Lazar Kosanovic, and on this date, 2nd October, 1992, he was your immediate superior; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 07036.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We object and we would object to this line of questions at all. This is our expert witness for destruction of religious sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The witness has testified repeatedly during both direct and cross that he was giving information on the basis of his personal knowledge. We explained in our notification of what we were going to challenge that we understood that much of his evidence was based on his personal knowledge, for instance --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But for evidence in connection of destruction of religious sites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but isn't it true that the composition of the unit was a major part of who were in the unit and that that is part of his expert report and that this may be relevant to complete that picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you think so, Your Honour, but we do not share that opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P7494. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7494 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Chamber has received evidence that Muslims detained at Manjaca were also impressed into assisting the engineers regiment in rebuilding, for instance, an Orthodox church at Sljivno. You're aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not up there, but I claim that these people were never part of the regiment. These men, as for this order that is written and what you're saying now --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it is possible that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, they were forced to assist the regiment. They weren't part of the regiment. They were prisoners; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying to you that the regiment was not dealing with the church at Manjaca. The church is right above the facilities where the people were held captive. The regiment never commanded --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- these people and never --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end of the witness's sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if could you first repeat the end of your sentence. You said: "The regiment never commanded these people," which, as far as I understand, was not suggested in the question. And then you said: "And never ..." and could you repeat what you said then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These people were never prisoners of the engineering regiment, and they were not used for carrying out work. It's a huge number of people; 110 people to be involved in working on a church? And the dimensions are, say, 8 by 8 metres, 8 by 10, or something --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to focus carefully on my question. We've moved passed this document, which is about the road company, the camouflage company, and the company building fortifications. What I'm putting to you now is you're also aware that people detained at Manjaca - prisoners there - were impressed into assisting the engineer's regiment in reconstructing a church at place called Sljivno. You know that; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I'm saying to you, do count these men: 121, 47, 110, 200 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to stop you. Was the engineers regiment involved in reconstructing a church in Sljivno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P238. Sorry, my notes on this may be inaccurate or this may not be P238. Based on the ERN, I can see it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any suggestion how to resolve it? Do we have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: By pulling up P238, which is what we have now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a 1st Krajina Corps order. We see it comes from General Talic. It's dated 22 August, 1992, on the basis of the demonstrated need to repair the Serbian Orthodox church in the village of Sljivno, and he is issuing this order. Point 2, he says: "The construction of an access road, preparation of the terrain, shall be carried out by the engineers of the 1st Krajina Corps ..." Point 3: "Professional instruction for and supervision of the construction shall be ensured by the construction service of the 1st Krajina Corps. Point 5: "The collection centre at Manjaca shall provide the workforce to carry out all the work on the site ..." Now, 22nd of August, 1992, by this point you were the commander of the engineering regiment. Can we take it this refreshes your recollection as to whether prisoners at Manjaca were impressed into assisting with the reconstruction of the church at Sljivno?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is possible. I'm just telling you one thing. The engineers regiment had nothing to do up there in relation to this approach road that had already been built. The church had been destroyed there. There were foundations there. It is construction people that were needed there; builders, bricklayers. As for the regiment, such a powerful unit, to engage them there, there was no need for that. This was not written by Lazar Kosanovic who was too much of a professional to write up something like this. Perhaps I sent a machine or two. But to remember 20 years later, that is virtually impossible. I'm just telling you that the regiment did not participate here. Just look here at the team that was appointed to carry out this work. There is no reference to the regiment. If 200 of my men were involved there -- or actually my men and 200 prisoners, people would have known about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Finally one more thing. At Manjaca --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please finish that sentence. At Manjaca, you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even at Manjaca you had an engineering unit within the school centre, so I had no need to be involved up there. You had bulldozers there and excavators and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That engineering units answered to Colonel Kosanovic, the one located in the school centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything down the professional line. After this order he could have said there's no need to send anyone up there because you've got that unit up there --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't understand the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last sentence which was not understood by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assumed that this was written from somebody from the command who doesn't know a thing about engineering. And when Kosanovic probably received this order, he said: "You have a unit, you have mechanisation, you have equipment up there. You've got everything and you can handle all that." And it was the commander of the school centre at Manjaca that had all that, because I never received from Kosanovic any such thing because he would have told me in that case to involve the regiment. Had Kosanovic written an order to me, he would have said: Send such-and-such and such a thing, or he would have asked me to reconnoitre to see what it was that I needed. This was written by a layperson, this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, a moment ago you said maybe I sent a machine or two. Now, you're excited --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, maybe. I cannot rule that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Could you please allow Mr. Traldi to finish his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So my point is now you've gotten visibly excited by the possibility and deny that there was any involvement of the engineering regiment, claim that anybody who would have written an order suggesting the engineering regiment be involved must not know anything about engineering, you are simply trying to exculpate yourself and your regiment and providing for the umpteenth time today evidence that you do not know whether it's true or not. That's what's going on; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not right. You're not right. You think that after 20 years, after 20 years -- well, maybe somebody called me and said, say, "Send an excavator up there" or something like that. Do you know how much that mattered to me at that moment? You know, you've got thousands of other tasks that are far more important and far more interesting. There's no war or anything in Manjaca, you see. But to link up an entire unit for the building of a little church, 7 by 8 metres, that is mind-boggling. And to send 200 prisoners to do that, that would have required a company of soldiers to guard them. And now this is what you're putting to me. That's why I'm saying I'm so sorry that I don't have my work notebooks that you took away and that was part of my war-time document, and probably now we could find very easily an oral order, say that Colonel Kosanovic sent to me, said "do such-and-such a thing." There were written orders, there were oral orders, and I wrote all of that in my work notebook only, and now you are expecting me, 25 years later, to remember where I sent which machine. That is ridiculous. Maybe I did send it, but I don't rule out that possibility. I cannot be unfair.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, in the future if you don't remember the answer to my question, I'd ask you to simply tell us that. And I have one more question before the break. You don't remember any of the myriad destroyed mosques and destroyed Catholic churches in the 1st Krajina Corps's area of responsibility being rebuilt during the war, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You do not remember any of the hundreds of destroyed mosques and destroyed Catholic churches in the 1st Krajina Corps's area or anywhere else that you saw in preparing your expert report being rebuilt during the war, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember just one. Very well at that. I remember when I was going down a road I saw these buildings destroyed and that really hurt me. Really afflicted me. And it was hard for me to communicate with soldiers of Croat and Muslim ethnicity who were at war with us, and buildings were being destroyed in the way they were being destroyed. I remember that full well. And believe me, these contacts were very hard for me, terribly hard for me. There were soldiers who would walk up to me and say: "What do we do now, commander?", you know? These are terrible things. And some idiot did what he did and committed the kind of things that were committed, and I can guarantee that I never was involved in any kind of thing. It's not that I am getting worked up or whatever it was that you said. I'm just trying to remember all of these things that you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And can you now please answer the question. Was there a single mosque or Catholic church rebuilt during the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, no. As far as I saw, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That could have been the short answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you started your answer by saying: "I remember just one." Which one do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, probably I am saying when I was passing by and I went to deal with different tasks and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have no recollection as which one you referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Could you refresh my memory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you to explain what you said, that you remembered just one, but apparently you don't remember where and when exactly. Before we take the break, I'd like to invite you to do the following. We considerably -- Mr. Traldi paid considerable attention to the Srebrenica mosque and the dates given by Mr. Riedlmayer which do not completely -- which are not completely reflected in your report. You said that some of the mosques were destroyed during combat and others were destroyed after withdrawal. Mr. Traldi asked you several times how you categorised the Srebrenica mosque, whether it was in your account -- well, one second, please. One second, please. In your -- whether, in your account, it was among the 10 or the 84. I'd like to know whether you considered the Srebrenica mosque as being destroyed during combat operations or after withdrawal, in which category you put this Srebrenica mosque. I take it that you have notes somewhere which would allow you to specify which ones are among the 10 - I think that was after withdrawal - and which one are under the -- no, the 10 during combat and which one are among the 84 which were destroyed after withdrawal. I'd like to know, on the basis of your notes, how you categorised the Srebrenica mosque. If you could try to find that out during the break, that would be appreciated. We take the break now. You're invited to follow the usher. We resume at ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you take your earphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to use the time, Mr. President, I can inform the Chamber and the Defence that the portion of 65 ter 32853 that I'd used with the witness has now been uploaded as 65 ter 32853A. And if the Defence has no objection, we'd request that that be admitted as P7493.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see from Mr. Lukic's body language that there is no objection. Mr. Registrar, you are hereby instructed to replace 65 ter 32853 by 65 ter 32853A, and P7493 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, before I return to my questions, before the break Judge Orie had inquired whether you were able to categorise the Carsijska Dzamija in Srebrenica, whether you were able to figure out whether you categorised this as having been destroyed during combat or after VRS withdrawal. Do you have an answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was during combat, around the 19th of July. As for what I've read now, I believe the army was still there. On that basis, I recorded it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You recorded it as having been destroyed during combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. No. The army was still there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but was it destroyed during --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, but there was no combat. No combat at the time. So the mosque was destroyed after combat. There was no combat in Srebrenica after that and it was recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither had the VRS withdrawn at that time from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I so assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so the original point that I'd been putting to you, that many of these mosques were destroyed not during combat and also not after VRS withdrawal but when the VRS had control of the area, that's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're wrong. As for some buildings, yes; but most of them, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But do you then agree that a third category is missing; that is, destroyed not in a combat situation when the Serb -- the VRS was still in control of the area? That's a third category which is ignored in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not ignored. When you look at Riedlmayer's report and witness statements and statements of the Islamic religious community, they say after the withdrawal of the army, after the population moved out, such-and-such and such happened, and that's most of the cases, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if only on the basis of this one example - I'm not talking about the others - you would have needed a third category. And the question that would arise then is how many other such incidents would fall into that category, and that's what I call ignoring that third option. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With that, I agree, absolutely. You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you discuss a number of sites in Prijedor, the Chamber has received evidence that the 43rd Motorised Brigade was based there. For a site that was destroyed after the end of fighting in Prijedor but while the 43rd Brigade was still based there, did you consider that to be destroyed during combat or after withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that all buildings after combat operations were over were destroyed not at the time when the area was under the control of the 43rd Motorised Brigade from Prijedor. That is correct. Because at that time the Prijedor Brigade was carrying out speedy preparations for Operation Corridor. If is somebody is trying to say to me here that the destruction of religious buildings was the priority of that brigade at the time, that's ridiculous. If anyone knows what the priority was at that time in Banja Luka and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm stopping you there. No one asked you about priorities. The question put to you by Mr. Traldi simply was whether mosques destroyed in the Prijedor area after the initial combat operations there, whether you agree that they were destroyed when the 43rd Motorised Brigade was still based there? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Part of the Prijedor Brigade were in brigade, not everybody left Prijedor. It was their home municipality, logistics was there for them. But to assert that at that time the entire area of responsibility, which was free, there were no Muslims there, why would the units of the Prijedor Brigade be in the villages? What would they be doing in the villages? What would be their role there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you apparently have found questions you consider more relevant than the questions that are put to you and which you consistently do not respond to. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your evidence about what the 43rd Brigade was doing, is that based on any study you did for this report or is it based on your recollection of events in 1992 from your time as a VRS officer; one or the other?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is already personal. In June 1993, I was in the field --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- for a month --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you. Is your evidence about what the Prijedor Brigade did, that you just provided, is that based on your study in preparing this report, or is it based on your memory of events, of facts that you remember learning during the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were referring to 1992, whereas the witness started his answer referring to 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm focusing on your evidence about its priorities in 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I keep telling you that my summary about the destruction of buildings after the combat was over was taken from the material that was analysed by Riedlmayer. But I am saying that in 1992, pursuant to a corps command order, I was in Krecane where the Prijedor Brigade Battalion was. The commander was Bojic. He's now in the Assembly of the B and H. I was at his command for a month as assistance, and so I was speaking with them at that time, that literally after the completion of the Kozarac operation and when the rifles stopped shooting and in view of the fact when the buildings were destroyed, you cannot link that up with the time that the Prijedor Brigade was there. The Prijedor Brigade was, throughout that period, based at the barracks in Prijedor. So it's very hard to separate that. You keep telling me that the Prijedor Brigade was there up until that time and then it went somewhere, but no. Actually, some units remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, this Chamber has received --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I again have to establish that the witness blaming you for telling him all kind of things, whereas you invite him to tell what he knows. The witness has not answered the question. Please, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, again, sir, I'm exploring your repeated assertions that many of these were destroyed after withdrawal. You just made that in regard to the Prijedor mosques. Now, the Chamber has received evidence about VRS operations in the Brdo area during the week of the 20th to 25th July 1992 in Prijedor municipality. You know from your review of the Riedlmayer report, I'm sure, that that report reflects the destruction of the Rizvanovici mosque, the Carakovo mosque, and the Brisevo Catholic church during that same period. Did you categorise those sites as destroyed during combat or after VRS withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number was destroyed in combat. The bulk was destroyed after the withdrawal of the VRS. If you take the date there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you focus on the three examples mentioned by Mr. Traldi. The first: Rizvanovici mosque. During combat or after withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was the date? I -- I can't answer just like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The 21st of July. The date, sir, if it assists, is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Traldi gave you the week of the 20th to the 25th of July, 1992. How did you categorise the destruction of that mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no combat at that time. It was finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Fine. So therefore it could not have been in combat. Was it after the withdrawal of the VRS from that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand your testimony to be that in the week of the 20th to the 25th of July, 1992, the VRS had withdrawn from the area where that mosque is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence from number of Defence witnesses who were in the Prijedor Brigade - Drasko Vujic, Miso Rodic - who testified that the brigade did carry out operations in the Brdo area during that period. You weren't in the brigade. As far as I can tell from your report, you weren't in Prijedor in 1992. Are those soldiers in the brigade wrong and you're right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the brigade's soldiers could have been doing in the villages and with the mosques in July and who had sent them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the truth. You don't know. You haven't studied any VRS documentation. You have no idea when the VRS was conducting operations in any particular area. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do know. I know when combat ended in Prijedor. It didn't last for three months. It was going on for 15 days. After that, there was no more combat there. There were groups of savages there who were doing what they were doing. That's the whole point of the story. As to whether that person wore a uniform or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's an answer perhaps to another question. After that period of combat in the Prijedor area, did the VRS withdraw from that area, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm saying again: A number of the war units did set off for the corridor operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking whether some troops left. I'm asking you whether the VRS withdrew from that area after these combat operations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know, you are asking me to specify for you the exact area from where the military withdrew, but the army was based in the barracks. It wasn't out in the field. It wasn't out in the villages. It didn't operate in the villages. This is what I'm talking about. As for somebody perhaps who stepped beyond the regulations, that's another thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I have to understand your testimony to be that after the combat operations in Prijedor, the army remained in the barracks and didn't leave the barracks and were not in control of that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The terrain was cleared, practically. So there were no more any elements against which it would be necessary to fight. The operation was completed. There were no combat actions once the clearing was over. There was no army in the villages. The mosques were mostly in the villages. As those who were wandering around, looting, going about, which groups, that's something that I cannot speak about. But as far as I know, the Prijedor Brigade -- there was none of that in the Prijedor Brigade as far as I know during the war and later. It's simply --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They were staying in the barracks and there was no need to be in the field because combat was over and therefore you would just stay in the barracks. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One follow-up question. Which army did have control over the villages in that area when the VRS stayed behind in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no able-bodied population once the operation was over. All that was left were women, children. All the able-bodied people were removed, so there was nobody to fight against. What sort of a danger did they pose?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question. Which army had control over these villages at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that it was the official organs, the police. The army had no business being there. The army had finished its job. You had the police, the legal organs, and so on and so forth. I guess that was part of their job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the simple answer to the question I'd originally asked you, sir, is your evidence is the Trial Chamber should believe you and not the Defence witnesses from the 43rd Brigade who testified that these operations took place. That's what you're asking the Chamber to do; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- well, it depends on what people say an operation was. I mean, if there was looting and robbery and so on during the operation, that was one thing, but it was not part of the combat operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask about two more examples. Novoseoci mosque in Sokolac, did you classify that as destroyed during combat or after VRS withdrawal? The date is the 22nd of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mosque in? Novoseoci, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. Did you classify that as destroyed during combat or after VRS withdrawal? Now before you answer, I see you're looking at Mr. Riedlmayer's report. That's because there is no place in your own materials where it says which mosques you claim were destroyed during combat and which you claim were destroyed after withdrawal; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I took exclusively Mr. Riedlmayer's data. I didn't have other data. I was not in Sokolac. I didn't go to Prijedor. I mean, I didn't go anywhere. I just went to two mosques which I analysed in detail. That was the Ferhadija mosque and the Petricevac monastery, nothing else. All the other data I took from the data of your expert. That's the point of the story. And on the basis of that, I wrote my own analysis. I didn't go into whether it was true or not. I wasn't interested in that. I just looked at what Mr. Riedlmayer had written. Had I wanted to deal with that, I would have needed two years to complete my report, not a week -- well, not seven days but seven hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Novoseoci mosque, which of your two categories did you put it into?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the combat was over, of course. I mean, even the date here indicates that. The date is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the Chamber has received the commander of the 2nd Romanija Brigade's report to the Main Staff and the SRK command that day - it's P3822 - and he reports that the village of Novoseoci was cleansed that day, and evidence in this case reflects that the male residents were massacred. Did you consider evidence like that in determining whether to list something as during combat operations or after, quote/unquote, withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I am repeating the same thing. You expect me in seven hours of work to look at all of those documents, the report written by a the commander of that unit. How could I have had access to that information? Mostly here I looked at the techniques, the manner, and the proportions of the building, the manner in which the building was demolished. This was something that was of interest in the -- the manner in which the former JNA, according to its regulations, would do something like that. As for what some commander wrote, well, that should have been presented to me, and then I would have given my opinion on that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask for a clarification. Sir, you say you had only seven hours to do this job and therefore you couldn't read the necessary material. Do we have to understand, therefore, that you have no evidentiary material before you upon which you base your professional opinion that 10 of the mosques were destroyed during combat and 84 were destroyed after the withdrawal of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all that information I tried, and I think I succeeded in covering, through Mr. Riedlmayer's report. I analysed his information. I did not go into whether the information was truthful or not. All I did was create an overview of what was destroyed when. I had no other information, and I didn't go into the truthfulness of the data. All I did is consider the report and what the witnesses told him on the basis of which he drafted the report, and mainly the sources were the Islamic community and some humanitarian organisations and trips to the field. I myself wasn't there. In order for me to go all of these 94 mosques and to look at them, I would have needed at least three or four months, and that would also take into account all the logistics required for something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me stop you there because you haven't begun to answer my question. I'm asking you about your opinion that you're giving this Court, that 10 of the mosques were destroyed during combat and 84 were destroyed after the withdrawal of the VRS, and I'm asking you: Do you have any evidence on which you base that opinion now that you're telling us you had limited time and you didn't read all the material that could have given you the information that you required to make that determination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Throughout the war, wherever there was combat, after certain terrain or towns were liberated, the army wouldn't stay there for five or ten days after that. Then the assistant commander for civilian affairs would be sent to that town, and then he would establish contact with the town authorities, and so on and so forth. That was the system of work. So the army had nothing to do in the terrain where there was no longer any enemy other than places where the lines were being held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm -- okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this was not the case in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have not asked you any question about the army or what it does after combat. You obviously are not answering my question. You may proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One last example.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 19777; page 69 in the English, 68 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is an entry in the diary of Nenad Davidovic, an officer in the VRS 6th Brigade in Sanski Most, which he authenticated during his testimony as a Defence witness. And we see here his notes of what he refers to as a command meeting with military officers on the 24th of June, 1992. Under Colonel Basara's name, we see that he refers to mopping up Hrustovo, Vrhpolje, Sanica, Gornji Budelj, and Donji Budelj, and below that we see details of different units' tasks. Those are villages in Kljuc and Sanski Most municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 02826.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a 1st Krajina Corps daily combat report from the 27th of June, 1992. Turning to page 2 in the English but still on page 1 in the B/C/S at point 3, we read: The mopping up and disarming of what are referred to as paramilitary units in the areas of Kotor Varos, Jajce, Prijedor, Kljuc and Sanski Most are continuing ... This is a report on the 27th. We saw the notes on the 24th identifying villages in Kljuc and Sanski Most, including Sanica. I'm going to put to you that present in Mr. Riedlmayer's formatted entry for the Sanica mosque but absent from your report is the destruction of the Sanica mosque on the 26th of June, 1992. Did you consider the Sanica mosque as having been destroyed during combat operations or after VRS withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? There are municipalities here. Does that mean, on the basis of this combat report, that the operations were being carried out in the entire territory of the Sana municipality or just in parts of the territory?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you know that? Sanski Most --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I asked you was a simple question: Did you classify the Sanica mosque as destroyed during combat or after VRS withdrawal. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say anything. I cannot say because there's the question of in which part of Sanski Most is combat being carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you classified 10 destructions against 84. What Mr. Traldi wants to know is how you classified this one. As simple as that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying again Mr. Riedlmayer analysed for each mosque where, what, before, after, so from this document, it's not possible to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you to comment at this moment on this document. How on the basis, as you said, of Mr. Riedlmayer's information, how did you classify this mosque: Being destroyed during combat or after withdrawal? Because that's what you're telling us in your report. Now whether there's a good basis for it or a bad basis, the first thing we would like to know is under what category falls this mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of statements by witnesses and the Islamic community gave to Mr. Riedlmayer for his report, but you cannot tell from this report because Sanski Most is a large territory. I don't know which village had fallen, which didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You say it is on the basis of Mr. Riedlmayer's information that you were able to classify the 10 against the 84. The simple question is: This mosque, was it destroyed during combat or was it destroyed after withdrawal? This one. How did you classify it, on whatever basis, but how did you classify it? Did you classify it under the 10 or under the 84?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly how Riedlmayer classified it, based on statements that he used to write his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Then I have another question for you. How did you understand Riedlmayer to classify this mosque, during combat or after withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need to read it again. I just need to find it. I need to look.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm happy to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P2510, page 173 in both languages. We're one page too ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So Mr. Riedlmayer's informant statement refers to information in the records of the Islamic communities. It says the Sanica mosque was set on fire on the 26th of June, 1992, and was completely burned out. All of the sacral objects inside the mosque were looted or burned. Then it says the minaret was blown up on the 1st of August, 1992. Where in that paragraph do you find any reference to VRS withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And where do you find that the VRS was in Sanica at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, sir, is that in coming to this conclusion you have essentially made numbers up. You have no basis for it, and you are providing the Trial Chamber information that you have no basis for providing. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm asking you where --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- does --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojkovic, you're not here to ask any questions to Mr. Traldi. That's one. And, second, Mr. Traldi is testing your evidence as we find in your report, and there's no need to ask Mr. Traldi what his position is as to the presence of VRS troops because it's you yourself who classifies the destruction of mosques in either of the two categories. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to turn now to my final topic, your opinion in your report that the destruction of these cultural sites was an uncontrolled spate, not part of the chain of command. So just to make sure I understand your evidence, it's your evidence that the violence committed against every Muslim and Croat cultural sites that either you or Mr. Riedlmayer looked at in these 12 different municipalities, different areas of Bosnia at different times, was either some sort of grassroots movement of people desecrating mosques and churches or a coincidence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you study the comments of any Bosnian Serb or Serb leaders about mosques and churches during the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which leaders you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, at the moment --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are speaking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I've asked a broad question. Did you study the comments of any Bosnian Serb or Serb leaders about mosques during the war in coming to this purportedly expert conclusion.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally believe that there was no need for that. As for these photographs, the way in which buildings were destroyed, and then the time and place where the destruction took place, I think that there is no comment needed by these people. This is classical spontaneity a whirlwind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we again -- you said you personally believed that there was no need for doing that. Does this mean that you did not study, you did not review the comments of any Bosnian Serb or Serb leaders about mosques during the war? Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how we have to understand your answer, that there was no reason to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All day I talked about this. I even asked Davidovic, the minister of religion in the government of Republika Srpska, just when the war was coming to an end and after the war, and I asked for some additional information. He claimed to me that the leadership of the Bosnian Serbs did not take part in this. And I even brought here a document that he wrote after the destruction of the Ferhadija mosque where he, as minister, addressed the public and condemned this criminal act. I talked to him for a long time. Almost an entire day I talked to him about this. And he even looked at this report of mine that I was writing. I asked him whether he should add anything to that or whether I should take away anything from that and he said that would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you consulted Mr. Davidovic to learn more about the attitude of the Bosnian Serb or Serb leaders. Next question, please, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 32844.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an article from the New York Times dated the 21st of August 1992 titled: "Serb Gains in Bosnia Create Chaotic Patchwork." Turning to the bottom of page 2 in both languages, we see a quote from Simo Drljaca, the chief of police in Prijedor. He says: "With their mosques, you must not just break the minarets. You've got to shake up the foundations because that means they cannot build another. Do that, and they'll want to go. They'll just leave by themselves." This is not the sort of statement that you would have considered in coming to your conclusion that the Bosnian Serb authorities were disconnected from the destruction of mosques, is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read this statement, but what are you trying to say with this statement? A man who was certainly an extremist, he did what he did, are you going to link his statement to the statements made by all the leaders of Republika Srpska; the state, military, and political leaderships?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I'm going to do, sir, is go through a few examples. Is it correct from your answer that you did look at this statement, didn't mention it, and concluded based on the conversation you had with Mr. Davidovic that you were going to suggest this wasn't policy. That's the approach you took as a purported expert; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If Simo Drljaca was chief of police in Prijedor and if he made this kind of statement, what happened on the ground refuted that. On the ground, there are buildings that were not destroyed in the manner that he described here. So if he said this, then he is a man who had to go and see all of that, check that, and give orders to carry that out, and that was not carried out at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not see that and your expert Riedlmayer didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, yet again you're refusing to answer my question. Is it the case, yes or no, that you failed to consider statements by actual authorities and relied on one conversation you had with a gentleman named Davidovic in coming to this conclusion. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I read quite a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, if you say -- and let me re-read your question: "Is it the case, yes or no," and then you finish your question by "that's the truth; right," that's not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I agree Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, it's correct that whether or not you looked at this statement, you didn't consider it in coming to this conclusion and instead relied on one conversation you had with a person named Davidovic; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First of all, I relied on Riedlmayer's report on the way in which buildings were destroyed, the ones that I dealt with in detail, and also what they looked like after the demolition, that this had nothing to do with the system, with orders, with carrying out orders. That is what I am speaking about. And now you quote Simo Drljaca who says what he says, and the situation on the ground is a direct opposite and that is the point. And you're not saying anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So first those two sites that you just said that you dealt with in detail, those are only two sites - the Ferhadija mosque and Petricevac church - neither of which come up in Mr. Riedlmayer's report; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For the 223 sites that Mr. Riedlmayer analysed, including his database, all you did was look at pictures of 94 of them; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Everything that was given to me, everything that was given to me by the Defence. I reviewed all of that. All the photographs. And I lost quite a bit of time there. There are some things there that are unimportant, but I went that you that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Focusing on the loss of time, you agree there were hundreds of mosques and Catholic churches in the 1st Krajina Corps's area in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I notice from your analysis of the Ferhadija mosque and the Petricevac church, that in your view to demolish the sites properly would have taken multiple days of preparation. You recall giving that evidence in your report; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now with a war on, it might well be the case that there were more pressing things for an engineering unit to be doing than spending two or three days looking at the plans of a building that it was going to demolish; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's just an assumption. Don't drag me into that. That's not fair. We never dreamed of such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what I'm testing, sir, is the basis --

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not destroy buildings of my soldiers. Do you think that I as commander would be destroying the buildings of soldiers who are waging war together with me? Does that seem logical to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not talking about logic, at least not any logic which is not within your realm of expertise, and we are talking about the facts. Would you refrain from putting questions and would you, rather, answer the questions. And would you also, Mr. Traldi, focus very much on -- to avoid composite questions, because it started all with what the witness had considered as far as statements of leaders are concerned. We still do not know whether he considered -- whether he was aware of and considered the statement as reported to have been given by Mr. Drljaca in a US newspaper. Did you know of that statement of Mr. Drljaca and have you considered it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew of it. I knew of it. I read it. But as for this expertise that I carried out, I found it to be unimportant related to the situation as it was on the ground after his statement was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You considered it not of such relevance to include it in your report but you were aware of it. Mr. Traldi, perhaps -- you announced more or less that you would have another few statements or --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to be put to the witness. I leave it in your hands to proceed as you consider wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll just ask one follow-up question. I know we're close to the time for the break, but perhaps I'll suggest to Mr. Lukic that we could agree on a couple of them during the break and save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, based on your analyses of the Pribicevac and Ferhadija sites and the hundreds of mosques and churches in the 1st Krajina Corps's area of responsibility, it's correct that to destroy those in the way that you suggest could have required a thousand or more days of time from various units in 1992 when they also had other tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's again a very composite question, Mr. Traldi. Could you try not to put everything together. First, it's about the number of days needed to do it. And then the other matter is the next question, then, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Though I've already asked both of those separately, and so the -- the total produced by the witness's previous answer -- previous answers is a significant amount of time. What I'm putting to him is that's a significant amount of time that would have been hard for the VRS to spend in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were to take an assumption because we were not the Army of North Korea or Boko Haram. I did not have problems like that, that somebody would force me to commit such a criminal act. I claim that no one could have done that, not General Talic, not anybody else. But I will tell you one thing: In the engineering regiment, I had a unit, a battalion of pioneers, about 600 men, and they were only mining and de-mining. Also, I had another pioneer battalion, same manpower, and they were only supposed to demolish tunnels, bridges, and so on. Military facilities, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, unfortunately again you're not responding to the question. One simple question: If you would have wished - I'm not saying that anyone wished that - but if you would have wished to destroy the churches and mosques within the area of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps, would that have taken considerable time if you would have used the methods as were prescribed in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had to do that? The first thing I would do, I would go to see all these buildings. I would carry out a detailed analysis, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, doing all that, would that have taken up to a thousand working days? If would you wish to do it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how many days would it have taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, a lot less because many buildings could have been demolished mechanically. In relation to that, there were public utility companies in different municipalities that could have been involved in such tasks, so you really could have reduced the time needed. I was just speaking of a particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you would have wished to blowup in the professional way as prescribed in the JNA instructions all of the churches and the mosques in the area of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps, how many days would have that taken? I'm not talking alternative ways of destroying them but if you had wished to blow them up in accordance with the rules. How many days would that have taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we talking about 100 buildings or how many or just these, the ones that Mr. Riedlmayer included in his report? Or all the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you assist me in a number given by Mr. Riedlmayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, actually, so, what I'd been putting was all mosques and Catholic churches in the 1st Krajina Corps's area, so that's beyond the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be what number, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Several hundred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Several hundred. Let's make it 300. If you want to blow up 300 churches --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One month, maximum. One month, maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many working days of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up to one month at the most, maximum, given the forces that I had; that is to say, not to involve civil engineering from civilian structures. If they were to be involved, then the time would be a lot less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With your people you would do ten a day. Is that -- if you wished to do that properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even more. Even more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what it would require for each site was the people to be involved to spend two or three days figuring out how to best do it; right? Set aside the total amount of time to get the job done with all the people for each site would require the people involved to spend two or three days to do it; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, during war time, as for documentation and looking at facilities -- I mean, everything was different. So that time would be a lot shorter. That would be no problem whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have to take a break, Mr. Traldi. Witness, you're invited to follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you give us an impression as far as timing is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I expect to finish before the end of the day regardless of whether we can agree on two of the other statements. And if I might just tender, so I don't forget, the two documents that I used but have not yet tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's 65 ter 02826 and 32844. And there's also a page from Mr. Davidovic's diary. I'm in the Chamber's hands whether we should admit the page separately from the parts that have already come in or add it to P7418, which is the current selection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any preferences in relation to the last question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whatever my colleague deems --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's clearly on the record where it comes from; therefore, I think it could be added to the selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you're not doing anything with 19777?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the page from Mr. Davidovic's diary. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 2826 shall be assigned Exhibit P7495. And 32844 shall be assigned Exhibit P7496. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7495 and P7496 are admitted into evidence. We resume at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, anything to report?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic has asked me to show the two documents in question, so I'll be very efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I need a couple of minutes at the end of this session as well. I'm -- we might go five or seven minutes, then, over the time if you are strictly adhering to the five minutes. And I ask the booth whether this would be a major problem for them. It's an urgent matter which I have to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that there's no -- at least no strong opposition from the booth and it's, as always, highly appreciated. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32856.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is part of a publication called Zapadna Srbija. We see it's published by the Serb Radical Party of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina. That's a nationalist party; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say so, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see and we've got in the bottom in the English and the bottom right in the B/C/S a cartoon of a mosque with an exploding minaret labelled "Castration of Islam." I'm going to show you one more example and then I'll have one quick question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32857.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. And this is another part of an issue of the same publication.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 3 in the B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what we see at the bottom, you see a cartoon of a man with a broom standing in front of an Orthodox church sweeping away buildings with minarets on them; right? You see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You didn't study publications by Serb nationalist parties in preparation for your report either, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't now and I did not do it before, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 32856 and 32857.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When were these cartoons published?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Both during the war; one in 1993, one in 1994. My notes say the first one in 1994 and the second in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 32856 shall be assigned Exhibit P7497. And 32857 shall be assigned Exhibit P7498.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7497 and P7498 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Finally, sir, the Chamber has received evidence in relation to specific mosques of both President Karadzic and General Mladic encouraging the destruction of mosques or saying, in Mladic's case, that: "A mosque with two minarets in the Tesanj area couldn't be left standing." You didn't study their statements in preparing your report either, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we object to this type of questions. It's too broad and the witness should know who, when, what was said. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, did you -- the objection is denied, Mr. Lukic. The -- did you review any report as suggested by Mr. Traldi; that is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. And I wasn't interested in that either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That completes my questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Lukic, may I take it that you want to re-examine the witness. And perhaps we should not start with it today. Could you give us an indication as to how much time you would need tomorrow for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope that I can finish in maybe a bit more than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Bit more than a half an hour. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to deal with another matter briefly. Witness, could I ask you: You drafted the report and you gave that to the Defence, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you prepare the text on a computer and did you add the photographs to it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, and I did have a computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you yourself inserted the photographs in your report so that the entirety of the report, was that what you delivered to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although I did have some additional things that I wanted to look at. However, the pressure was such I had to submit it urgently, so because of the time restraints I wasn't able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If would you please focus on my questions. So you delivered or sent the -- your report, including all the annexes, as one document to the Defence or was it split up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I contacted them, and then I took the parts from Riedlmayer's report that I thought I would need, and then I put it all together and sent it to the Defence. I tried to round it off and make a whole of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps -- excuse me. Perhaps I didn't cite that things were from Riedlmayer's report, but that is understood. It's implied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm mainly interested in this moment in the integrity of the report. You sent it as one report to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the lawyer, Mr. Lukic, has that information. I really -- I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you. Because if you sent it from your computer, it might still be somewhere in your "sent" box.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I submitted it to the Defence team in Banja Luka. I submitted the complete document in printed form, and I also submitted it on a USB, and then they sent it to the Defence team. I didn't send it directly myself. And I have here -- the person who received the documents, I have his signature here that I presented -- I submitted such-and-such a document to him. This is the person who works in Banja Luka for the Defence team headed by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us the name of the person that received the hard copy and the electronic version. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mikajlo Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you remember -- can you see that from the signature on what date it was delivered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2nd of February, 2015.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you ever receive it back or did you receive any comments on the report as you had given it to -- in Banja Luka to Mr. Mitrovic, I think you said? Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't know any of this until the Registry got in touch with me. About five days ago, perhaps. I didn't even know when I would testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Had you delivered previous versions of your report before February 2015?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Mitrovic asked me if I had done anything, I would submit things to him, but I told him that it wasn't finished. That's correct. I sent him an electronic version of parts of the report, and then the pressure was on to complete it. There wasn't enough time, simply. I am not in a position, in the material sense, to be able to do things like this, especially not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm mainly seeking to establish what happened rather than why it happened. Those parts you had sent or had given to Mr. Mitrovic, did you ever at a later time change those parts or did they remain untouched by you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps something was changed. Perhaps. When I provided Mitrovic with an integral hard copy version. Perhaps something was changed. It's possible. I can't remember exactly what, but it's possible. I worked on it and I knew that I would be coming here, so I continued studying some material. It's possible that something was added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But was it added after you had given it in hard copy and in electronic form in February to the Defence or ...?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After the 2nd of February, 2015, I did not change anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the content ever discussed with the Defence on the basis of the final version or the previous versions that were given in part to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I sent it. I think Mitrovic looked at something. I asked him that we look at it in more detail together, because I was doing a specific type of work in that case, but he said he didn't have any remarks to make, and I said all right. Other than the written -- the task that was written out of what I was supposed to do from Mr. Lukic, I had a lot of trouble how to round it off, how to present it. It's not easy with 100 demolished mosques. You get a little bit -- you're a bit stumped. You don't know how to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I'm taking you back to the issue that you were questioned about earlier; that is, about the Carsijska Dzamija Srebrenica municipality mosque. You remember that we had -- in the B/C/S we had four photographs. You remember? One on top, one below it, and then two. Do you have any recollection -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe the witness should take off his headphones. I checked that with my Case Manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off -- first of all, do you understand the English language? Could you take off --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- your earphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Everything went through our Case Manager. I really met this gentleman only once in Banja Luka in 2014, and the first time I saw him again when he came here to The Hague. Our Case Manager said that he was receiving some additions later, and originally there were only three pictures, as in English. That's why we have English version with three pictures. Not four. Later on the fourth one was added, and that's why we have fourth one in B/C/S, but everything else should be the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- so that's not CLSS's mistake either. [Overlapping speakers]... we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least good to know. And if you leave it to me for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you put on your earphones again. And could we have the relevant page? Mr. Traldi, you certainly will have the -- I may find it easily, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which report, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the English report --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's D1183.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I think it's page 149.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 149, yes. Could we have that on our screen. That seems not to be the right page in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wasn't it 142?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's 142 in the B/C/S. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I'd given the English page number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we can do with this one only. You see the -- in the B/C/S version that is on the left -- it must be on your screen. You see the second photograph without any subtitle? You see that one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you earlier told us that three pictures were good enough and that you didn't need the fourth one. Is that still your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGIC GOJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. When I looked at it, I thought that I had kept it out. And now that I see this photograph, I find that to be of interest to me too.
